audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers published Skill / Heimerdinger / Heimerdinger / Skill / Skill / Heimerdinger / Heimerdinger while the packet reads Heimerdinger / Skill / Heimerdinger / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Heimerdinger. Four rows disagreed — and two of them disagreed with this page's own prose: whys[4] ends 'Gragas owns the level-6 dive' under a row that said Skill, and whys[5] says 'he reclaims the first-item window' under a row that said Heimerdinger.
audit.why: Level 1 is mildly Heimerdinger's (one turret beats a single Body Slam start), level 2 is genuinely even because Happy Hour sustain undoes the beam chip, Heimerdinger owns level 3 and shares 4-5, then Explosive Cask at 6 and a Rylai's-plus-tank first item both belong to Gragas before the siege game tilts back at two items.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 4 and 5 flipped in both layers as one atomic paired group, with ratings re-cut and the phase whys rewritten to state the actual reason for each stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5] named Liandry's Torment as the spike to force fights on, and phases[4] said 'Upgraded E or W deletes his all-in'. First item and level 6 are both Gragas's stages in this lane.
audit.why: Explosive Cask is 100s at rank 1 and its knockback is the single displacement that beats an immobile champion's whole zone-control plan. Gragas's Rylai's-plus-tank first item lets him soak beams behind Drunken Rage while Happy Hour refunds the chip.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Explosive Cask with its 100s cooldown; phases[5].why states the brawl-through-poke item spike; phases[6].why states the real late-game reason Heimerdinger recovers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's entire interaction content was 'His engage. E-stun after it.' with no cooldowns and no mention of what actually beats Heimerdinger here.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s — barely shorter at rank 5, so a whiffed or spent E is a long, reliable punish window and that number makes the advice concrete. Drunken Rage is a 5s auto-attack reset that also reduces damage received, which is why poking immediately after his W cast is wasted. And CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stuns only a unit DIRECTLY hit while merely slowing the splash — 'E-stun after it' hides that the centre must land on him.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d now carry the 14s and 100s numbers and the direct-hit-stuns / splash-slows split.

edits.before: One turret + AA wins level 1 against almost everyone. Identify how Gragas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: One turret and no stun — but his single Body Slam can't out-trade your turret start either, so deny his last-hits.

edits.before: Three turrets make your half of lane a no-entry zone. Only take the trade when Gragas's Body Slam is down.
edits.after: Your second H-28G and the beam form the zone, but Happy Hour sustain keeps it even — don't poke into his heal.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gragas must walk into your range.
edits.after: Three banked charges plus the beam out-tax his Body Slam dives — every E he commits is damage he must heal back.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Body Slam's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His brawl matches your nest once Drunken Rage and Happy Hour are up — it comes down to whether your stun or his slam lands first.

edits.before: Upgraded E or W deletes his all-in — choose per fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Explosive Cask (100s) knocks you clean out of your nest, and a dashless yordle has no answer to the displacement.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Body Slam's cooldown.
edits.after: Rylai's plus a tank item lets him brawl through poke — he reclaims this window and shoves in.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Gragas carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: You out-scale as sieger and anchor: the super-turret holds towers he can't break and grenades punish any Cask engage.

edits.before: Build MR — turret-poke, E-stun his E-Q. Heimerdinger wins the Body Slam cooldown windows.
edits.after: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 — stun him inside the nest, then dodge Explosive Cask at 6.

edits.before: Build MR and E-stun his combo. Track Body Slam before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Own levels 2-5 with the nest and CH-3X, then track his 100s Explosive Cask — nothing else moves you.

edits.before: Gragas wins by landing Body Slam, denying your pattern, and out-trading your engage windows.
edits.after: Gragas wins by Casking you out of your nest, then brawling through poke on Drunken Rage.

edits.before: His engage. E-stun after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 — punish him for the whole window.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Your grenade stuns a direct hit and only slows the splash.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES: 'Hold Explosive Cask' (wants.foe[1]) and "Drunken Rage's" (late) are Gragas's real R and W names — the matcher fired on the leading verb and on the possessive apostrophe. No edits made for either. The content layer here was already accurate and specific; the defects were the four wrong chart rows (present in BOTH layers, so the two agreed with each other but not with the packet or with their own neighbouring prose) and a full layer still running the generic 'track his signature cooldown' template with no numbers. NOT ASSERTED: whether Explosive Cask's knockback can be Flash-buffered out of, and whether the CH-2 grenade stun interrupts Body Slam mid-charge or only lands after he arrives — neither is answerable from Riot's text, and the second one materially changes the level 4-5 trade pattern.
